properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 8:03PM CST until November 8 at 2:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Bandera County in south central Texas...
Southeastern Real County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Uvalde County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 200 AM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 803 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Vanderpool, Garner State Park, Rio Frio, Concan and Utopia.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to rise in Action Stage. The river is forecast to climb into Minor
flood stage late Sunday with a continued rise through Minor flood
stage anticipated through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.2 feet, Water completely surrounds many homes in the
Stone Island and Still Brook subdivisions. Pool enclosures and
patios become flooded. Water covers many of the roads. Flooding
occurs on Enterprise Road and in the Bethel Loop subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue rising to 6.3 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.0 to 3.2 feet through the middle of the week.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 7 at 8:39PM AST until November 9 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, mostly in Aguada
and Rincon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Through Sunday, a north to northeast swell
will build seas between 3 and 5 feet across the Atlantic
waters. This will increase the risk of life- threatening rip
currents across most exposed beaches along the Atlantic
coastline of Puerto Rico.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 7 at 3:23PM AKST until November 10 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong system is expected to move through the area Sunday night
into Monday. Temperatures below freezing combined with snow levels
below 1,000 ft are indicative of snowfall for upper elevations. Mid-
level southeasterly flow suggests potential for White Pass to be
sheltered from much of the precipitation, putting them on the lower
end of the range. A band of precipitation looks to set up across the
Fairweather and Chilkat mountain ranges, increasing the likelihood of
the Haines Highway seeing periods of heavy snowfall on Monday.

* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 6 to 12
inches possible.

* WHERE...Haines Borough and Klukwan and Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The upper elevations of the Haines Highway
near Haines Customs and the Klondike Highway near White Pass.
Higher amounts expected for the Haines Highway.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 7 at 2:19PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near the
water, especially those who will be participating in razor clam
digging.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding expected.
Additionally, dangerous rip currents and surf of 3 to 6 feet
expected along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest tides will occur in the late
morning each day, peaking at 7.4-7.6 feet Sunday and Monday,
which is 1.3 to 1.6 feet above astronomical tide predictions.
Surf will increase to 4-7 feet Monday, which may prolong some
of the coastal impacts.
properties.instruction:

If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Central Coast of Oregon
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 7 at 12:35PM PST until November 8 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement on the beaches, sneaker
waves possible. For the High Surf Advisory on the beaches, large
sneaker waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 28
feet.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late tonight.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 11 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will result in widely scattered tree damage

properties.instruction:

if you were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 7 at 11:41AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves 22 to 24 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 10 PM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide with
high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This will
allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 11:41AM PST until November 8 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24
feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between
8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM to noon PST
Sunday. High tide is at 10:21 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous surf
conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly
discouraged!

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide with
high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This will
allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.

will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 11:38AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06
AM Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,

properties.areaDesc: Zapata; Jim Hogg; Brooks
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 7 at 11:34AM CST until November 9 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of locally heavy rainfall are expected between
Saturday night and early Monday morning across the Rio Grande Plains
and Brush Country.  The first round is most likely between midnight
and mid-morning Sunday, when 1 to 2 inches with locally 3 or more
inches of rain may fall. The second round is expected Sunday night
into early Monday morning, when an additional 1 to 3 inches with
locally 4 inches or more may fall.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Deep South Texas, including the following
counties, Brooks, Jim Hogg and Zapata.

* WHEN...From 6 PM CST this evening through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos and
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Some
arroyos may rise out of their banks near where heaviest rains fall.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Highest concern

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 7 at 12:22AM CST until November 9 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the most experienced
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. These rip currents

properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 1:39AM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 10 to 16 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.1 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
